assertions.name: 1_every_live_site_is_classified
assertions.detail: 0 live divergent site(s) carry no ledger row. A new transcription cannot land silently: it lands here as unclassified.

assertions.name: 2_no_orphan_ledger_rows
assertions.detail: 0 ledger row(s) no longer match a live site. Expected transiently while a migration lands; drain them in the same commit so the ledger shrinks with the corpus.

assertions.name: 3_every_row_is_well_formed
assertions.detail: class in ('a', 'b', 'c', 'd'), substate in ('a-migrated', 'a-blocked') iff class a, non-empty reason, unique key. Offenders: 0 class, 0 substate, 0 reason, 0 duplicate.

description: The defect/non-defect split the families audit's own `caveat_not_split_source_vs_doc` asks for. Of its divergent SITES, only class (a) -- the literal feeds arithmetic or is published as a q0 -- are defects. Class (b) constants must NOT be migrated: the code names a superseded or held-fixed value in order to detect or reproduce it, and re-pinning one breaks the detector.
computation_method: Reuses hardcoded_q0_literal_families_audit.scan() -- it does NOT re-scan, so the two audits cannot disagree about which sites exist. Joins the live divergent set against the committed ledger q0-literal-classification.json on (file, literal) and checks completeness, orphans, row shape and declared counts. Pure string and set work; no arithmetic, no float64.
q0AnchorReason: Reads no substrate value as an input. It joins two string sets and computes nothing from any q0.
scope: scope-(a) MEASUREMENT plus a curated ledger. It classifies; it changes no literal and asserts nothing about which value a producer SHOULD carry -- that is the A-vs-C anchor question, an owner matter (ruled 2026-08-22, landing in PR #5500).

result.verdict: Quoting the families audit's divergent total as a defect count overstates it. The non-(a) classes are not tidiness debt: a class-(b) constant is load-bearing precisely BECAUSE it is a superseded value, and migrating one silently disables the check it powers.

context.anchor_ruling: Owner, 2026-08-22 (PR #5500): 'A --> CODATA 2022'. The families audit measures divergence against A, which that PR replaces with C = q_muon_at(). The char-13 family here is B (CODATA 2018), which #5500 declares out of its own scope. So the DESTINATION of a class-(a) migration is in motion, which is why most class-(a) rows are `a-blocked` rather than fixed here: reading the anchor is right under A and under C, but retyping either is right under neither for long.
